newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BASKET DEALS DOMINATE LIGHT BUDAPEST FX TRADE.
newsitem.headline: BASKET DEALS DOMINATE LIGHT BUDAPEST FX TRADE.

text.p: Basket deals in the dollar and mark accounted for almost all of low turnover on the Budapest forex markets on Friday.

On the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), March deals for the U.S. and German units in proportion to their 30/70 proportion in the central bank's currency basket accounted for 3,000 of the 4,318 lots traded.
The March mark fell 0.20 to 198.80 forints while the dollar for the same month rose 1.70 to 203.70.

Basket deals, under which the dollar and the mark are sold or bought in proportion to their weight in the central bank's currency basket against which the forint is floated, are a means of hedging against large fluctuations in the dollar/mark cross.

The forint is seen as steadier against the basket than against either of the two currencies which make it up -- 70 percent the mark and 30 percent the dollar -- and the Hungarian unit tends to stick close to the upper end of the 4.5 percent-wide intervention band.
In smaller the financial futures section of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) only mark and dollar futures changed hands, with one basket deal for September and four deals for the June 1998 mark.
The mark fell for December and next June by 0.19 and 0.15 to 116.08 and 123.80 forints respectively while the December dollar rose 0.34 to 198.01 forints.
